title: Outage: the model provider's account out of credit; every call refused from 02:53:57 (five were refused before 02:39 and taken for wrong answers); what stopped and how the stop was written down
summary: Dinis (~02:50): "you can use up to $20 in budget." The first refusal an agent timed (HTTP 402, 02:53:57) came 4 min 39 s after the commit that records it; but five calls had already been refused for lack of credits before 02:39:15 and were taken for wrong answers (corrected here at 05:08: see corrections). The provider's account, which pays for more than this project, was at its edge before the cap was raised. The cap is what the team may spend; the balance is what the account can pay. Nobody had been reading the second.

What stopped: every call through tools/llm.mjs. Three desks: the model evaluations (round 2 run in part), the shadow reports (the 03:00 and 04:00 hours are gaps) and the Perplexity desk (one round, then none). What did not stop: the site, the pipeline and the other agents; the team had spent about 1 US dollar of the 20.

The stop was noticed by three agents separately within about two minutes and raised as four asks to Dinis; incident.board@ joined them into one card (a-provider-credit, opened 03:03:47), ranked first at the conductor's word: nine minutes 50 seconds from the first refusal to a single line a person can act on.

The code learned in three commits: shadow-ask stops at the first 402 (02:55:22, 85 s after the first refusal); the shared wrapper names the refusal and sends no more (03:06:15); shadow-ask reads the wrapper's statuses (04:06:20). Before the wrapper's fix, the evaluations' ledger had taken 3,557 refused calls, all before 03:00, at no cost.

Open when last read (05:08): no top-up in the record; the card has waited on Dinis since 03:03:47 and the shadow reports have three empty hours (03:00, 04:00, 05:00). Only he can close it. Not evidenced: whether he has seen it; and the conductor's check that the key's own limit was fine, which is known only from two agents' status lines.

shape.step: n, at (UTC; for a commit step, the committer time), at_note, actor {name, kind: person|agent|ci}, in, out, handoff {to, via, evidence_of_handoff}, kind, sha (a commit of this repository unless repo says otherwise), agent_trailer, for[] (the commit's For: trailers), evidence[] (commit | version | file | url), evidence_note
shape.evidence: commit {sha, url}; version {version, run, own_run, served_by, push_to_served_s}: the first CI tag at or after the commit; file {path, section?}; url {url, read_utc}. Entries with "filled": true are written by tools/reporter-fill.mjs from git and data/ci/runs/. evidence: [] with evidence_note means the record holds none.
shape.handoffs: Messages between sessions are not in the repository. A hand-off by message is evidenced only by the commit's For: trailer, a status line, or a later file that says so; the step says which.
shape.person: A person's step is where Dinis acted. His words are known only as incident.conductor@ wrote them down in BRIEF.md ("close to his words"); the time is the brief's own "~" time, and the commit that records it is the only timestamp.
shape.names: The provider (OpenRouter) and the third-party models called through the ledger are named because they are the subject here.

corrections.was: The first summary line and the title said the first model call was refused at 02:53:57, "five minutes after the cap was raised", as if the account ran out after Dinis's word.
corrections.is: 02:53:57 is the first refusal an agent timed. Five calls had been refused for lack of credits earlier, in results incident.models@ pushed at 02:39:15, about ten minutes before the commit that records the new cap; they were counted as wrong answers until the evaluations page corrected it. The account was at its edge before the cap was raised. Step 13 is added for it at the end: step numbers do not change.
